findings.passage: That may simply be the market talking. It is also the 2015 move in reverse. Eleven years after "Now I have less fun. I focus more," the fun is back on the plan, chosen in a meeting by a man who learned as a teenage salesman that the attitude is part of what you sell.
findings.problem: The article closes on its most perishable material: a career direction stated on a podcast released March 31, 2026, set against Mercy's reception. By 2028 to 2031 his slate will have confirmed or contradicted that plan. The record already holds signals pointing the other way, and the ending doesn't mention them: The Terminal List season 2, an action series, premiered October 21, 2026 (src-fox-2026), and Variety reported the same day that Pratt confirmed Star-Lord's return (src-variety-2026). If the action roles keep coming, the closing image reads like a failed prediction instead of a portrait. "The 2015 move" also misdates the trade. By the article's own chronology, the weight came off after the Moneyball audition and before Zero Dark Thirty (2012) and Guardians (2014). 2015 is when he described it to GQ. Separately, c-mercy cites only Wikipedia for "a critical and commercial failure". Independent reporting I checked supports it (roughly 20 to 25 percent on Rotten Tomatoes; about $53 million worldwide on a reported $60 million budget, per GamesRadar and ComicBookMovie), but the record should not rest on the tertiary source.
findings.acceptance_test: The closing paragraph dates the plan to the March 2026 interview, and its insight holds whether or not his post-2026 lead roles are comedies. The point should be how he treats fun as a strategy decision made with his manager and agent, not a forecast of his filmography. "The 2015 move" becomes wording that either dates the trade to the years before Guardians or calls it the trade he described in 2015. c-mercy cites at least one non-Wikipedia source for the reviews and box office. c-comedy-turn and c-ending-interp carry a concrete check, e.g. "By October 2028, compare his announced lead roles with the stated comedy turn; if action dominates, revise the closing paragraph."

A scan of the body finds no present-tense attribution of a pre-2026 remark without a year nearby.

assessment: Five-year test: pass for the thesis, minor maintenance for the edges. The discriminator (protect the image, pay in fun) rests on GQ 2015 and Vanity Fair 2017, and the argument stands with every 2026 event removed. The 2026 Not Dead Yet material is retrospective biography, not news, so leaning on it does not date the thesis. Dates are almost all absolute and check out: 47 in June 2026, Jack nine in mid-2022, eleven years from 2015 to 2026, Parks 2009 to 2015. The FAQs lead with fixed dates (born June 21, 1979; married since June 2019), and their changing counts are tracked as time_sensitive. The perishable parts sit at the edges. The orientation ends on a present-tense Terminal List status, and the closing paragraph rests on a stated March 2026 comedy plan that the record's own October 2026 action signals already complicate; the Mercy-flop context is supported by independent reporting but cited to Wikipedia alone. A few dated remarks are written in the present tense. The evidence record has review triggers on its time-sensitive claims, but none on claims that depend on open research tasks, including Faris's remark, which the draft names as one of its two weightiest pieces of evidence. The podcast carrying about fifteen quotes is linked through a fragile mp3 download endpoint. Similarity advisory: not tripped (max 0.06, Dhar Mann). The top pairs share only type-definition vocabulary (heart triad, shame, "read a room and become it", also in Ben Shelton's page). Pratt's actual argument, the salesman frame and the fun-versus-image discriminator, is specific to him. No reuse finding. Risks: sensitive allegations (Page/Zoe Church, the Faris divorce) and contested typing (medium confidence, with 7 and 9 live) remain flagged; no major thesis change.
